newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden details 20 bln skr in pending plans - agency.
newsitem.headline: Sweden details 20 bln skr in pending plans - agency.

text.p: The Swedish government plans to spend more than 20 billion crowns by the end of 1998 on measures to stimulate employment and education, according to a copy of Tuesday's government budget obtained in advance by the national news agency TT.
Despite the new spending plans the government said it would achieve its goal of balancing the books by 1998, TT reported.
The budget deficit for 1997 was estimated at 2.1 percent of GDP.
The government said in the leaked budget that 4.0 billion crowns would be granted to local authorities this year to boost spending on healthcare and schools. That amount would be doubled in 1998.

In addition, the government would reveal in the budget a five point programme of labour market measures, further education, sustainable growth, improving business confidence and healthcare that will cost 16.3 billion crowns in 1998, TT said.
It reported the government said the increased spending would be financed by a projected budget surplus of 13.9 billion in 1998.
The government would spend 1.6 billion crowns on reducing employers' charges and subsidising environmentally friendly agriculture, TT said.
The cost of the government's five-point programme would grow to 21 billion crowns in 1999 and 23.3 billion crowns in 2000, sponsored by the country's budget surplus, the leaked budget said.
The government aimed to have a budget surplus of 0.5 percent of GDP in 1999 and 1.5 percent in 2000, the news agency said.
